alex: Hey team — I'm starting on-call next week and want to make sure I have everything. Can someone confirm what groups I need access to and where the on-call runbooks are?

maria: Welcome aboard, alex! You should be in the `redwood-oncall` SSO group and have read access to the `oncall-runbooks` Confluence space. I'll add you to the rotation once DevOps confirms the pager config.

devops-bot: Automated check: user alex not in group redwood-oncall. Please request access via https://idp.example.com/request and include your manager.

alex: Thanks — requested access just now (ticket #IDP-482). Also, who should I ping for pager escalation playbook questions?

oncall-trainer: @alex I'll run a 1:1 ramp session Wed 11am PT. We'll walk through the most common alerts, how to run the local repro test, and how to use the runbooks. Bring your laptop; I'll share a checklist.

kevin: Quick tip — clone the oncall-utils repo and run `./scripts/fake-incident --local` to practice. It simulates an alert and walks you through the CLI steps.

alex: ran the script, got an auth error when attempting to post to the test channel. Error: "403 Forbidden: missing scopes"

devops-bot: Bot notice: test-token for alex expired. Use `auth renew --service slack-test` or request a new token from infra-team if that fails.

maria: If renew fails, @kevin can temporarily create a support token. Also, check that you have the Slack app scopes: chat:write, channels:read.

sara: FYI for escalation — primary SRE on-call is paged first, then platform, then product-eng. Escalation matrix is on Confluence: https://confluence.example.com/display/ONCALL/Escalation+Matrix

oncall-trainer: For runbooks, start with the "API gateway 503s" doc and the "disk-pressure" checklist. They include exact commands (kubectl, node-restart) and RTO/RPO expectations. Link: https://confluence.example.com/display/ONCALL/Runbooks

alex: Got it. One more: how does rotation handoff work? I saw something about a weekly pairing schedule.

maria: Rotation is weekly, Mon 9am -> next Mon 9am. Handoffs are asynchronous: update the oncall-handoff doc and post a summary to #eng-oncall-handoffs with any ongoing mitigations. For critical incidents, call the next oncall phone after posting.

kevin: Also add a short note about any suppressed alerts and why — helps the next person.

alex: Access request approved! I can see the runbooks but still can't send test alerts. Trying `auth renew --service slack-test` now.

devops-bot: auth renew complete. Token issued and scoped.

alex: Test alert succeeded, and I joined the mock incident. Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the training on Wed.

oncall-trainer: Great — I added you to the pairing rota for Thurs 2pm with sara. We'll do one simulated P1 and one P2.

maria: Welcome again. If you hit anything weird before Wed, DM me or @devops. :thumbsup:

kevin: One last note — read the postmortem TL;DRs in the incidents space from the last 3 months. Good signal on what to expect.
